thread:
jon: anyone else seeing a sudden p95 jump on small-window text-gen? started ~15:12 UTC, qps steady but tails doubled :thinking_face:

deepa: yup saw it, i'm digging. profiler shows a repeating kernel-selection churn — kernels flip every 8-12s for the same model id. adding top lines:
```
[2026-03-17T15:12:04Z] kernel_selector: evaluate(model=redwood-7b, seq=64) -> candidate=[cuda_fast, cuda_fallback]
[2026-03-17T15:12:04Z] kernel_selector: choose cuda_fallback (score diff 0.02)
[2026-03-17T15:12:12Z] kernel_selector: re-evaluate due to perf-probe -> choose cuda_fast
[2026-03-17T15:12:20Z] kernel_selector: re-evaluate -> choose cuda_fallback
```

maria: KV cache metrics line up with this — kv_miss_rate spikes right when kernel hops. sample: `kv_miss_rate: 0.02 -> 0.18` around the same window. suspecting cache eviction when a new kernel pipeline warms up.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scale_action suppressed (reason="provision-threshold-hop") for pool=starter-bridge; backoff=30s; queued=12

jon: that autoscaler message is key. looks like the provisioner is doing small burst adds, each new instance triggers model kernel warm path and evicts local KV shards, leading to thrash. starter-bridge scale policy has min_idle=2 which is too small for bursti workloads. repro command for local canary: `./bin/provisioner --pool=starter-bridge --scale-probe=aggressive --log-level=debug`

deepa: confirmed on canary. also saw high PCIe latency on host gpu-3 during the spikes: `nvlink_latency_ms=4.8 -> 48` and device metrics show competing memcpy workloads (noisy neighbor).

devops: scheduled quick reassignment of pods from gpu-3 to other hosts, TTL 10m. also bumped min_idle to 8 on starter-bridge as a temporary mitigation. monitoring now. :white_check_mark:

maria: temporary routing tweak applied: `kernel_sticky=true` for model=redwood-7b to force reuse of last-chosen kernel for 30s. early numbers show p95 down ~20%. still need a proper fix in the selector heuristics (reduce sensitivity for marginal score diffs).

jon: action items: 1) deepa to add a hysteresis window in kernel selector to avoid flipflop on <5% score diffs (PR planned), 2) infra to run perf test with min_idle=8 and burst load, 3) devops to run a host-level sweep for noisy memcpy jobs and add placement constraints, 4) SRE to open incident doc.

infra-bot: incident created -> #inc-2103456789 (type: autoscale + perf-regression)

deepa: attaching flamegraph (link) and a short perf log in the incident doc. I'll open the PR for selector hysteresis later today.

jon: thanks all — good catch getting autoscaler + kernel + KV correlation. we'll follow-up in postmortem with perf traces and a bench to avoid regressions. :memo:
